`src/cli.js` is the program; how the work is split across other files under `src/` is up to you. It takes exactly one argument, `merge`, `merge2` or `regions`, and reads three documents from standard input. Split the input on newlines and drop the empty tail a trailing newline leaves; a line that is exactly `%%%` separates the documents, and every other line belongs to the document it sits in. The three documents, in order, are mine, the base they both derive from, and theirs. A document may hold no line at all. Exit 0 when the merge is clean and 1 when any conflict was written, on every mode.

Compare each side against the base with a longest common subsequence over whole lines, comparing them as exact strings. When two subsequences are equally long, take the one whose matches come earliest: walking both documents from the start, take a match whenever the two current lines are equal, and otherwise advance the side whose remaining subsequence is at least as long as the other's, preferring to advance the base when they tie. Every stretch the subsequence does not cover is a change, described as a run of base lines replaced by a run of that side's lines; an insertion replaces zero base lines and a deletion inserts zero lines.

Gather the changes from both sides into one list ordered by where they start in the base, with the changes from mine before the changes from theirs when they start at the same place. Walk that list: take the first remaining change, let the region run from its base start to its base end, and keep absorbing the next change while that change starts at or before the region's current end, extending the end to cover it. The base lines before a region and after the last one form stable regions, which the merge keeps unchanged.

A region only one change touches resolves to that side's lines. For a region several changes touch, each side's replacement runs from the smallest start of its own changes, moved back by however far the region begins before those changes do in the base, to the largest end of its own changes, moved forward by however far the region ends after them. With mine's lines, the base lines of the region, and theirs's lines in hand: if mine and theirs are equal the region resolves to mine; otherwise if mine equals the base it resolves to theirs; otherwise if theirs equals the base it resolves to mine; otherwise the region is a conflict.

`merge` prints the resolved lines in order, and writes a conflict as the line `<<<<<<< mine`, then mine's lines, then `||||||| base`, then the base's lines, then `=======`, then theirs's lines, then `>>>>>>> theirs`. `merge2` writes the same thing without the `||||||| base` line and the base's lines. `regions` instead prints one line per region: `stable N`, `mine N`, `theirs N` or `both N`, where N counts the lines the region resolves to and `both` names a region where the two sides made the same change, or `conflict mine=A base=O theirs=B` with the three line counts.

A failure writes one line to standard error and exits 2, having written nothing to standard output. The messages are `error: usage: cli.js merge|merge2|regions` when the argument is not exactly one of the three mode words, and `error: expected three parts separated by %%%` when the input does not hold exactly three documents. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root. This task is also judged on inputs you do not see: a validator runs your program on its own held-back cases and compares the exit code and output byte for byte. The visible tests cover the main paths only. Implement the written specification, including every corner it states, rather than the behaviour the visible tests happen to pin down.

You implement one program task in the workspace you are given, against its own test suite, and you stop when the tests pass.

The workspace is your working directory: every bash command and every file path resolves inside it, so read and edit its files by their relative paths and never search outside it.


Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

1: #!/usr/bin/env node
2: /**
3:  * The command. `node src/cli.js merge`, `node src/cli.js merge2` and
4:  * `node src/cli.js regions` each read three documents from standard input and
5:  * report the three-way merge of the second into the first and the third.
6:  */
7: 
8: import * as readline from 'readline';
9: 
10: // Parse arguments
11: const mode = process.argv[2];
12: if (!['merge', 'merge2', 'regions'].includes(mode)) {
13:   process.stderr.write('error: usage: cli.js merge|merge2|regions\n');
14:   process.exit(2);
15: }
16: 
17: // Read input from stdin
18: let input = '';
19: const rl = readline.createInterface({ input: process.stdin });
20: 
21: rl.on('line', (line) => {
22:   input += line + '\n';
23: });
24: 
25: rl.on('close', () => {
26:   try {
27:     processInput(input);
28:   } catch (err) {
29:     process.stderr.write(`error: ${err.message}\n`);
30:     process.exit(2);
31:   }
32: });
33: 
34: function processInput(input) {
35:   // Parse documents
36:   const parts = input.split('%%%\n');
37:   if (parts.length !== 3) {
38:     throw new Error('expected three parts separated by %%%');
39:   }
40: 
41:   // Parse each document
42:   const parseDoc = (part) => {
43:     if (part === '' || part === '\n') return [];
44:     const lines = part.split('\n');
45:     if (lines[lines.length - 1] === '') {
46:       lines.pop();
47:     }
48:     return lines;
49:   };
50: 
51:   const mine = parseDoc(parts[0]);
52:   const base = parseDoc(parts[1]);
53:   const theirs = parseDoc(parts[2]);
54: 
55:   // Compute changes for each side vs base
56:   const mineChanges = computeChanges(mine, base);
57:   const theirsChanges = computeChanges(theirs, base);
58: 
59:   // Merge and output result
60:   const { output, hasConflict } = performMerge(mine, base, theirs, mineChanges, theirsChanges, mode);
61:   process.stdout.write(output);
62:   process.exit(hasConflict ? 1 : 0);
63: }
64: 
65: // Compute LCS with early-match preference
66: function computeLCS(a, b) {
67:   const n = a.length;
68:   const m = b.length;
69: 
70:   // Build DP table for LCS length
71:   const dp = Array(n + 1).fill(null).map(() => Array(m + 1).fill(0));
72:   
73:   for (let i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
74:     for (let j = 1; j <= m; j++) {
75:       if (a[i - 1] === b[j - 1]) {
76:         dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1] + 1;
77:       } else {
78:         dp[i][j] = Math.max(dp[i - 1][j], dp[i][j - 1]);
79:       }
80:     }
81:   }
82: 
83:   // Reconstruct LCS with early-match preference
84:   const lcs = [];
85:   let i = n;
86:   let j = m;
87: 
88:   while (i > 0 && j > 0) {
89:     if (a[i - 1] === b[j - 1]) {
90:       lcs.unshift({ i: i - 1, j: j - 1 });
91:       i--;
92:       j--;
93:     } else {
94:       // When sequences are equally long, advance the side with at least as long remaining
95:       // Prefer to advance base (j) when they tie
96:       if (j > i) {
97:         j--;
98:       } else {
99:         i--;
100:       }
101:     }
102:   }
103: 
104:   return lcs;
105: }
106: 
107: // Convert LCS to list of changes
108: function computeChanges(side, base) {
109:   const lcs = computeLCS(side, base);
110:   const changes = [];
111: 
112:   let lastSidePos = 0;
113:   let lastBasePos = 0;
114: 
115:   for (const { i, j } of lcs) {
116:     // Create a change for the gap before this match if there is a gap
117:     if (lastSidePos < i || lastBasePos < j) {
118:       changes.push({
119:         baseStart: lastBasePos,
120:         baseEnd: j,
121:         sideStart: lastSidePos,
122:         sideEnd: i,
123:         side: side.slice(lastSidePos, i)
124:       });
125:     }
126:     lastSidePos = i + 1;
127:     lastBasePos = j + 1;
128:   }
129: 
130:   // Handle trailing gap if there is one
131:   if (lastSidePos < side.length || lastBasePos < base.length) {
132:     changes.push({
133:       baseStart: lastBasePos,
134:       baseEnd: base.length,
135:       sideStart: lastSidePos,
136:       sideEnd: side.length,
137:       side: side.slice(lastSidePos)
138:     });
139:   }
140: 
141:   return changes;
142: }
143: 
144: // Perform the three-way merge
145: function performMerge(mine, base, theirs, mineChanges, theirsChanges, mode) {
146:   // Merge the change lists
147:   const allChanges = [];
148:   
149:   mineChanges.forEach(change => {
150:     allChanges.push({ ...change, source: 'mine' });
151:   });
152:   
153:   theirsChanges.forEach(change => {
154:     allChanges.push({ ...change, source: 'theirs' });
155:   });
156: 
157:   // Sort by base start position, with mine before theirs when equal
158:   allChanges.sort((a, b) => {
159:     if (a.baseStart !== b.baseStart) return a.baseStart - b.baseStart;
160:     return a.source === 'mine' ? -1 : 1;
161:   });
162: 
163:   // Process regions
164:   const regions = [];
165:   let lastBaseEnd = 0;
166: 
167:   while (allChanges.length > 0) {
168:     const firstChange = allChanges.shift();
169:     let regionBaseStart = firstChange.baseStart;
170:     let regionBaseEnd = firstChange.baseEnd;
171:     const touchingChanges = [firstChange];
172: 
173:     // Absorb overlapping changes
174:     while (allChanges.length > 0 && allChanges[0].baseStart <= regionBaseEnd) {
175:       const nextChange = allChanges.shift();
176:       touchingChanges.push(nextChange);
177:       regionBaseEnd = Math.max(regionBaseEnd, nextChange.baseEnd);
178:     }
179: 
180:     // Add stable region before if needed
181:     if (lastBaseEnd < regionBaseStart) {
182:       regions.push({
183:         type: 'stable',
184:         lines: base.slice(lastBaseEnd, regionBaseStart)
185:       });
186:     }
187: 
188:     // Separate changes by source
189:     const mineInRegion = touchingChanges.filter(c => c.source === 'mine');
190:     const theirsInRegion = touchingChanges.filter(c => c.source === 'theirs');
191: 
192:     // Resolve the region
193:     if (mineInRegion.length === 0) {
194:       // Only theirs changed
195:       regions.push({
196:         type: 'theirs',
197:         lines: assembleReplacement(theirsInRegion)
198:       });
199:     } else if (theirsInRegion.length === 0) {
200:       // Only mine changed
201:       regions.push({
202:         type: 'mine',
203:         lines: assembleReplacement(mineInRegion)
204:       });
205:     } else {
206:       // Both sides changed - resolve conflict
207:       const mineLines = assembleReplacement(mineInRegion);
208:       const theirsLines = assembleReplacement(theirsInRegion);
209:       const baseLines = base.slice(regionBaseStart, regionBaseEnd);
210: 
211:       if (arraysEqual(mineLines, theirsLines)) {
212:         regions.push({
213:           type: 'both',
214:           lines: mineLines
215:         });
216:       } else if (arraysEqual(mineLines, baseLines)) {
217:         regions.push({
218:           type: 'theirs',
219:           lines: theirsLines
220:         });
221:       } else if (arraysEqual(theirsLines, baseLines)) {
222:         regions.push({
223:           type: 'mine',
224:           lines: mineLines
225:         });
226:       } else {
227:         regions.push({
228:           type: 'conflict',
229:           mine: mineLines,
230:           base: baseLines,
231:           theirs: theirsLines
232:         });
233:       }
234:     }
235: 
236:     lastBaseEnd = regionBaseEnd;
237:   }
238: 
239:   // Add final stable region if needed
240:   if (lastBaseEnd < base.length) {
241:     regions.push({
242:       type: 'stable',
243:       lines: base.slice(lastBaseEnd)
244:     });
245:   }
246: 
247:   // Generate output based on mode
248:   let output = '';
249:   let hasConflict = false;
250: 
251:   if (mode === 'merge' || mode === 'merge2') {
252:     regions.forEach(region => {
253:       if (region.type === 'stable') {
254:         output += region.lines.map(l => l + '\n').join('');
255:       } else if (region.type === 'mine') {
256:         output += region.lines.map(l => l + '\n').join('');
257:       } else if (region.type === 'theirs') {
258:         output += region.lines.map(l => l + '\n').join('');
259:       } else if (region.type === 'both') {
260:         output += region.lines.map(l => l + '\n').join('');
261:       } else if (region.type === 'conflict') {
262:         hasConflict = true;
263:         output += '<<<<<<< mine\n';
264:         output += region.mine.map(l => l + '\n').join('');
265:         if (mode === 'merge') {
266:           output += '||||||| base\n';
267:           output += region.base.map(l => l + '\n').join('');
268:         }

Implementation complete and all tests pass. Summary of what I changed:

**`src/diff.js`** (new) — LCS over whole lines:
- Suffix DP table `table[i][j] = LCS(side[i..], base[j..])`, then a **forward** walk from the start exactly as specified: take a match when the current lines are equal, otherwise advance the side whose remaining subsequence is at least as long, base winning ties. (The old code reconstructed backwards with a bogus `j > i` heuristic — the main source of wrong output.)
- `changesAgainstBase` turns the uncovered stretches into `{baseStart, baseEnd, sideStart, sideEnd}` changes, covering pure insertions and deletions.

**`src/merge.js`** (new) — region building and resolution:
- Changes from both sides sorted by base start, mine before theirs on ties; regions grow while the next change starts at or before the current end; stable regions fill the gaps and the tail.
- For multi-change regions, each side's replacement is computed by the specified stretching rule (smallest side start moved back by the region's lead, largest side end moved forward by the region's trailing overhang), and a side with no change in the region keeps the base lines. The old code just concatenated change lines, losing the surrounding context lines.
- Resolution order: mine==theirs → `both`, mine==base → theirs, theirs==base → mine, else conflict.

**`src/cli.js`** — driver:
- Mode validated first (exactly one argument, one of the three words) before any input is read; errors write one stderr line, nothing to stdout, exit 2.
- Input is now split on newlines with a single empty tail dropped, and documents are separated by lines that are *exactly* `%%%` (the old `split('%%%\n')` on the raw text also matched `%%%` at the end of a longer line, and readline silently added a missing trailing newline).
- `merge`, `merge2` (no base section) and `regions` rendering; exit 1 whenever a conflict was written, 0 otherwise. Writes use a partial-write-safe `writeAll` so nothing is truncated before `process.exit`.

Checks run: `node --test test/*.test.js` → 15/15 pass; manual edge cases (adjacent changes forming one conflict, rival insertions at the same spot, empty base, empty document, input without a trailing newline, extra argument); a 20k-case fuzz confirming mine/theirs symmetry; and a 20 000-line input smoke test. No `node_modules`, no files outside `src/` touched.
